results.statement: sc-lint's dependency ownership check (global_dependency_ownership) must limit enforcement to source files only when a consumer opts in through a setting, and otherwise keep checking all files.
results.quote:
sc-lint enforces dependency ownership on source files only, and we know which of atm-core's three boundary settings it already covers.
Definition question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "is source-only enforcement the default behavior, or an opt-in setting?" Rand: "opt-in"
results.context: Phase M planning; Rand approved the sentence and answered 'opt-in' to the definition question, relayed by team-lead 2026-10-30 (lint-xccm)
results.deterministic_check: A boundary test shows that, with the source-only setting on, an ownership violation in src/ is reported and the same import in a tests/ target is not; with the setting off, both are reported.

criteria.yes: It concerns this dependency ownership rule or its scope setting.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` touch global_dependency_ownership, SCB-MANIFEST-004, or their ownership-scope configuration? Judge subject overlap only.

criteria.no: It omits this behavior, merely mentions the topic, gives incompatible behavior, or (for delivered work) defers it.
criteria.unclear: It describes a possible scope mode but leaves whether it has the required opt-in/default behavior ambiguous.
criteria.yes: The description states both opt-in source-only checking and otherwise all-files checking.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` say the complete ANC-025 behavior is planned or preserved: source-only ownership enforcement requires consumer opt-in through a setting, while absence of opt-in keeps all-files checking? Judge the stated behavior only.

criteria.no: No stated behavior conflicts with the required conditional behavior, including silence or deferral.
criteria.unclear: The described behavior could conflict but is too ambiguous to decide.
criteria.yes: It makes source-only automatic/default, removes the opt-in option, or fails to check all files without opt-in.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly prescribe or report dependency ownership behavior incompatible with requiring a consumer opt-in for source-only checking and keeping all-files checking otherwise? Silence and deferral alone do not establish incompatible behavior.
